examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Function Given in Implicit Form Using the Product Rule
examples.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y = y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $xy$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ (x+2y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x-y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x-y}{x+2y}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(y)+3{x}^{2} & =11 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{log}⁡(y)+3{x}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{log}⁡(y))+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{1}{y\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})+6x & =0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-6x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(-6x)(y\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)\,xy\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
